# Why the Iran War Is Stuck & What Comes Next with Steven Cook

First listed: 2026-08-12 | Evaluation cutoff: 2026-11-10

[Back to library](../README.md)

## Source versions

- [Substack: Why the Iran War Is Stuck & What Comes Next with Steven Cook](https://realeismanplaybook.substack.com/p/why-the-iran-war-is-stuck-and-what) - 2026-08-12

Earliest listed publication among matched versions, not proof of an unedited contemporaneous archive. Claim timestamps refer to the reviewed version.

## Summary

Cook explains the Iranian regime survival, contested Hormuz navigation and fragmented regional responses. He expects the conflict to remain stuck three to four months after the July 28 recording. Early November maritime reports support that persistence forecast. Eisman endorses the impasse and challenges confidence in Iranian promises. The discussion also covers Saudi transformation, Syrian incentives for accommodation, Lebanese disarmament and Turkish influence. Private motives and military inventories remain largely unverified; a new UAE pipeline reduces crude-export exposure without establishing economic immunity.

The central dated guest forecast has observable support. Most causal claims rest on private contacts or strategic interpretation, so they remain unresolved. Eisman closing endorsements are separately coded. Legal custom is distinguished from constitutional text.

## Framework and tools

- Separate tactical destruction from strategic capitulation.
- Identify regime survival incentives rather than assuming civilian economic pain changes leadership behavior.
- Distinguish material depletion from having no stock remaining.
- Analyze regional states separately rather than as one bloc.
- Use infrastructure alternatives to assess commodity exposure without assuming complete immunity.

Tools and charts discussed, not a complete visual inspection:

- Recording date July 28, 2026
- Leadership casualties and missile/interceptor stocks
- Hormuz transit restrictions, blockade and proposed tolls
- UAE bypass pipeline and OPEC membership
- Regional military coalitions and security agreements
- Saudi social and economic reforms
